_comment_purpose: Patterns are TEMPLATES, not finished regexes: the loader substitutes the
placeholders below before compiling. This is deliberate — the anchor-matching
patterns depend on the live domain list in config/taxonomy.yaml, and freezing a
literal domain alternation into this file would create a second source of truth
for the taxonomy that silently desyncs the moment a partition is added.
_comment_substitution: SUBSTITUTION IS .replace(), NEVER str.format(). Three patterns contain literal
regex braces — heading's {1,6}, admonition_indent's {4}, and admonition_status's
literal '{status:' / '\\}' — which str.format() would either raise on or silently
mangle. The loader performs exact token replacement of every placeholder listed
under `placeholders`, then rejects ANY surviving brace-wrapped identifier: an
unknown token such as {node_id} is a valid regex (Python treats a non-quantifier
brace group as literal text), so it would compile cleanly and then match nothing,
reporting the resulting empty corpus as a legitimate one.

placeholders.domain_alt: Alternation of every re.escape()d `domain` in config/taxonomy.yaml, sorted longest-first.
placeholders.role_alt: Alternation of every re.escape()d entry in document_roles below.
placeholders.file_role_alt: Alternation of every re.escape()d entry in file_naming.roles below.
placeholders.locale_alt: Alternation of config/corpus_layout.yaml filenames.locale.values (mode: suffix), or the empty string (mode: none).
placeholders.locale_sep: '\.' when config/corpus_layout.yaml filenames.locale.mode is 'suffix', else the empty string. Always written immediately before the locale group, so mode 'none' compiles to an empty locale group.
placeholders.extension_pattern: config/corpus_layout.yaml filenames.extensions: '\.md' for a single extension, '(?:\.md|\.markdown)' for several.

_comment_placeholders_layout: locale_alt, locale_sep and extension_pattern come from config/corpus_layout.yaml,

_comment: QUARANTINED SECTION — DO NOT UNIFY THESE WITH `patterns` ABOVE.
ingest.py's check_likely_typos() uses these two DELIBERATELY PERMISSIVE
patterns to emit WARN-only nudges: they match a line that looks like it is
TRYING to be an anchor or a ref callout but does not match the real grammar —
most often a typo'd domain such as ^specint-001. The author then finds out at
ingest time instead of discovering months later that a block was silently
unindexed.
Their looseness is the entire point. They accept [A-Za-z0-9-]+ where the real
grammar accepts only a KNOWN domain. 'Tightening' them to the strict patterns
would make them match only VALID anchors, so check_likely_typos() would warn
about nothing and the diagnostic would be silently lost — no error, no test
failure, just a check that stopped checking.
They take no placeholders and are compiled as literals.
Explicitly NOT extracted into this file: parse_graph.py's _TAG_RE,
_WHITESPACE_RE and _SPACE_BEFORE_PUNCT_RE. Those are HTML-stripping and
whitespace-normalizing helpers inside plain_text_summary() — rendering
internals, not AST grammar. Externalizing them would put presentation-layer
mechanics into a file the linter treats as the domain contract. Likewise the
repair-tool patterns in fix_markdown.py / fix_domain_typo.py and the tag
patterns in extract_public.py: those tools are deliberately loose in their own
distinct ways and are not part of the parse contract.
validate_markdown.py defines no regexes of its own — it derives everything
from graph_lib.py. Confirmed by grep; nothing to extract there.
DECLARATIVE FILE-NAMING VALIDATION (Task 1).
THE ROLE SEGMENT IS OPTIONAL, AND THAT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE WITH THE CORPUS.
The brief specified ^.+\.(contract|debate|ops|evi)\.[a-z]{2}\.md$, which
makes the role MANDATORY. Tested against the live corpus, that pattern
rejects 100% of real filenames -- 01-architecture-overview.en.md,
000-template.vi.md and every other file predate the split-file
convention and legitimately carry no role. graph_lib.document_role_of()
documents this explicitly: a None role 'is never missing a role, it
simply predates the convention'. Enforcing the brief's pattern verbatim
would emit 56 warnings on a clean build.
LOCALES AND EXTENSIONS ARE NOT DECLARED HERE. They come from
config/corpus_layout.yaml (filenames.locale, filenames.extensions) through the
{locale_sep}, {locale_alt} and {extension_pattern} placeholders, the same values
file discovery uses. A naming rule wider than discovery would PASS a file the
compiler never sees -- a silently dropped document; one source removes that gap.
A 'locales' key here is rejected at load time as a duplicate declaration.
THE ROLE SEGMENT FOLLOWS THE SLUG: (?:\.(?P<role>...))? before the locale segment.
It accepts the same names as the earlier \.(?:(?P<role>...)\.)?(?P<locale>...) form
and also compiles when the layout declares no locale segment at all.
`roles` HERE IS DELIBERATELY NOT `document_roles` ABOVE. document_roles
drives SPLIT_DOCUMENT_RE, which MERGES sibling files into one logical
document. Adding 'evi' there would make incident-2026-05.evi.en.md a
sibling of incident-2026-05.en.md and fold its content into that
document's node set -- the opposite of Task 3's intent that evidence
stands alone as unindexed prose. This list is for naming validation only.

SLUG EXCLUDES DOTS ([^.]+, not .+?). With a lazy .+? slug, a MISTYPED role segment silently reabsorbs into the slug -- '01-x.contarct.en.md' matches cleanly as slug='01-x.contarct' and nothing is reported, which makes the whole role whitelist unenforceable. No filename in the live corpus contains a dot in its stem, so excluding dots costs nothing and turns a typo'd role into a diagnostic.
REF-GATED PAYLOAD LOCK POLICY (Task 2). Declarative boundaries for the
pre-commit hook. NOTHING ENFORCES THESE YET -- see FINDING 4. The
compiler is a pure read-model builder and never writes to docs/; a lock
is a WRITE-path concern and therefore belongs in a Git hook, which does
not exist in this repo today.
The state machine the hook implements, per anchor:
unreferenced -> body mutable, frontmatter mutable
referenced   -> body IMMUTABLE, only mutable_frontmatter_keys may change
A node becomes referenced the moment any [!ref-<anchor>] resolves to it,
which graph_lib.find_orphan_refs() already computes as a side effect.
INDEPENDENT DEPENDENT-NODE LIFECYCLE (Task 3). Everything the dependent
state machine needs, declared rather than hardcoded. graph_lib.py loads
this via config_loader.load_dependent_lifecycle() at import time.
WHY NO `status_values` KEY HERE: the dependent lexicon is THE SAME closed
set as `status_values` above, not a second copy of it. A duplicate list
would be a second source of truth for one closed set -- exactly the
failure mode this config extraction exists to remove. `strictness_order`
below is validated to be a PERMUTATION of `status_values`, so adding a
sixth status up there without ranking it down here raises at import
instead of silently producing an unrankable value at compile time.
`anchor_reference_fields` IS A NAMESPACE DECISION, NOT A DETAIL. At
DOCUMENT level (Tier 3) `superseded_by` carries a document_id -- see
graph_lib.document_metadata_from_text(). On a DEPENDENT-ROLE file it
carries an ANCHOR id (Tier 4), because what a deprecated dependent needs
to point at is the rule that replaced its parent, not a document. Those
are two different namespaces sharing one key name, distinguished only by
the file's role segment. That is a real smell, and it is declared here
rather than hardcoded precisely so the alternative -- a distinct
`superseded_by_anchor` key -- is a one-line config edit and not a code
change. If you take that option, add the field to this list and to
conditional_requirements.deprecated together.
UNINDEXED PROSE TOLERANCE (Task 3). A file with zero parsed contract
nodes already compiles as ast_valid=false / status='ast_non_compliant'
with a non-fatal [WARN] -- that behavior predates this config and is
verified, not newly built. This section makes the SEVERITY configurable
per partition rather than fixed at 'warn' in Python.
'fail' is honoured by validate_markdown.py's strict mode only. The
compilers stay non-fatal regardless: a compiler that refuses to emit a
graph because one document is unanchored would take down the whole
corpus for one incident log.
CONFIGURABLE VOCABULARY. `aliases` maps the AUTHORED token in
`> [!<token>-<anchor>]` to an INTERNAL dependent role. The token is
user-facing and free; the role is the closed set the JSON schema, the
frontend and dependent_lifecycle.dependent_roles are all keyed on.
Rename `ref` to `cite` here and the corpus changes; graph.json does not.
`kind_alternation_sort: length_desc` for the same RE2 reason as domains.
`suffix_letters` supplies the composite-id letter per role, so no letter
is spelled in Python. `separator` must not be in [A-Za-z0-9-] or a
composite id would be indistinguishable from a plain anchor.
`subblock_letters` is the CLOSED set of hierarchical suffix letters.
It must be a superset of suffix_letters' values; 'c' (clause) has no
dependent role and exists only as an authored sub-anchor. Narrowing this
set is what keeps `^spec-lte-01-002-x99` from being read as a child.
